key_decisions.decision: MODE fixed at elaboration (parameter) vs runtime input
key_decisions.ma_choice: Elaboration-time parameter; only the selected boundary policy is built
key_decisions.plan_choice: Compile-time parameter; only the selected overflow logic is generated (D9)

key_decisions.note: Both default to WRAP. The encoding difference does not change the architecture.

key_decisions.plan_choice: Illegal MODE handled by an elaboration-time error, and the handling is documented

key_decisions.ma_choice: MAX = 2^N-1 (all ones), derived localparam; no modulus parameter

key_decisions.note: The spec gives load over counting. Reset priority is a convention.

key_decisions.ma_choice: load acts whenever load=1, regardless of en
One shared N-bit adder: count + (up ? 1 : all-ones)
Natural modulo-2^N overflow of the adder; no extra compare
key_decisions.plan_choice: WRAP uses natural overflow; no compare for the count update

key_decisions.decision: SATURATE implementation and sharing with tc
key_decisions.ma_choice: Suppress the update when en && at_bound (up ? at_max : at_zero); tc = at_bound, so the same signal is reused
key_decisions.plan_choice: SATURATE suppresses the update using the boundary compare, which is the same signal as tc

key_decisions.decision: tc timing: combinational decode vs registered
key_decisions.ma_choice: Combinational decode of count_q and live up; TC_REG is only a future option
key_decisions.plan_choice: Combinational decode; TC_REG is a future extension (D2, per Q1)
key_decisions.note: The spec's 'registered outputs' is ambiguous for tc, so asking was justified.

key_decisions.ma_choice: tc ignores en and load; it is a pure boundary indicator
key_decisions.plan_choice: tc depends only on count and up (D3)

key_decisions.ma_choice: Single cycle, single register, flat with no submodules
key_decisions.note: The plan does not mention submodule partitioning, but the structure is the same.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Single rising-edge clk, synchronous active-high rst, en as a datapath enable, no CDC
key_decisions.plan_choice: Single rising-edge clk, sync active-high rst, no clock gating (D10)
Minimum legal N stated (N=1 covered); no upper bound defined
key_decisions.note: Only the documentation of the bounds differs.

summary: The plan matches the reference MA on essentially every architecture-level decision: compile-time MODE, MAX = all-ones, rst>load>en>hold priority, load independent of en, a shared ±1 adder with natural wrap, a SATURATE hold that reuses the tc boundary compare, tc as an unqualified combinational decode, and a single-cycle synchronous design. The differences are minor and equivalent: MODE is encoded as a string rather than an integer (both default to WRAP), and no explicit upper bound on N is given. The single question (Q1, registered vs decoded tc) was justified, because the spec's 'registered outputs' is ambiguous for tc.
